title: How to Talk With Tenants About Safety Without Overpromising (Video)

findings.quote: Under California Civil Code section 1946.8, a lease can't limit a tenant's right to call for help, and a landlord can't penalize them for it.
findings.root_cause: The script and legal takeaway omit the statutory conditions for protected calls; see §1946.8(b)–(d) and parent finding 10195-F02.
findings.fix: Script replacement: “Third, don't discourage calls for help. California Civil Code section 1946.8 protects calls about abuse, crime or an emergency when the caller believes help is needed. A lease can't restrict those calls, and a landlord can't penalize a tenant or resident for them.” Key takeaway replacement: “Civil Code §1946.8 protects calls about abuse, crime or an emergency when the caller believes assistance is necessary; lease restrictions and landlord penalties for protected calls are prohibited.”
findings.future_prevention: Apply 10195-F02 to both scripts and the video key takeaways.

findings.quote: A security report is notice: reply the same day, fix it, log it and watch for patterns
findings.root_cause: The legal-resource context makes an unlimited notice statement and a same-day response instruction sound statutory. Same-day handling is documented AEBP policy for broken entry/lobby locks, not a universal legal repair deadline. Distinguish it from general best practice and §1941.3.
findings.fix: Key takeaway replacement: “Best practice: acknowledge security reports promptly, assess urgency, arrange needed repairs and document follow-up. Reports of covered lock deficiencies can provide notice under Civil Code §1941.3.” Fourth script paragraph: “Fourth, as a best practice, acknowledge security reports promptly, assess the urgency, arrange needed repairs and keep a record. A report about a required lock can give notice under California's lock statute; other reports may raise different duties.”
findings.future_prevention: Preserve the documented AEBP same-day policy in its own paragraph; label the general workflow as best practice.
